title: Schema-first streaming adapters for cursorless pagination and cross-SDK retry semantics
creator: Maya Chen
description: Deliver a spec and acceptance criteria for a schema-first adapter layer that lets client SDKs expose streaming model outputs as memory-bound, paginated iterators without requiring a persisted server-side cursor. The adapter must define cross-language retry semantics, backpressure behavior, and fragmentation rules so Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs implement interoperable behaviors with minimal user surface changes.
background: Several customers have asked for an easier path to integrate long streaming LLM outputs into existing paging-based UI patterns (infinite scroll, segmented displays) without having to manage server-side cursors. Existing Linear tickets focus on cursors, resumable streams, and paged iterators but assume a cursor exists server-side. This ticket explores a client-side adapter approach that composes streaming frames into page-like units using a shared schema and consistent retry semantics across SDKs.
requirements: Spec: define a canonical framing schema for stream events (meta, fragment, error, end) that is language-agnostic and compact
Adapter API: SDKs must expose a PaginatedStream abstraction with has_next()/next_page() patterns in Python/TS/Go and an async streaming iterator that yields Page objects
Memory and latency bounds: each page must be emitted as soon as it reaches either a token count limit, time threshold, or full semantic boundary (sentence/JSON chunk), configurable per client
Retry contract: transient network or worker failures should allow automatic in-flight resume with idempotent semantics and at-most-once downstream emission unless user opts into deduplication helpers
Backpressure: clients must support configurable buffering and observable metrics for dropped/queued tokens; default SDK behavior must prioritize low memory usage
Compatibility: new adapter must not break existing cursor-based APIs; fallback to server-side cursors when present; server responses that include cursors must be treated as authoritative
Interoperability tests: cross-SDK test harness must validate identical page boundaries given the same framing stream and config
Telemetry: SDKs must emit events for fragment reassembly time, retry triggers, and page emission latency for Console dashboards
scope_changes: Initial scope included building server-side persistent cursor support — scope reduced to client-side adapter + fallback to existing cursor responses
Removed on-prem pluggable router integration from MVP; will be handled by Dedicated team separately
Limited SDK surface to unified PaginatedStream abstraction; advanced helpers (deduplication library) deferred to follow-up ticket
decisions: Adopt a schema-first framing DSL: each stream message must include a 1-byte tag + length-prefixed payload to simplify cross-language parsing
Default page boundaries: prefer semantic boundary (newline/JSON record) + 4k token soft cap + 500ms time cap, all configurable

Retries: use short-lived resumable offsets embedded in stream metadata instead of persistent server cursors. If server supplies a full cursor, prefer server cursor and expose to client via Page.cursor
Backpressure: SDKs will expose a max_buffer_tokens config; if exceeded, SDK will pause upstream polling and surface an on_high_backpressure telemetry event
Compatibility: do not change existing endpoints; adapter will be implemented client-side and be opt-in via sdk.paginated_stream_enabled flag
acceptance_criteria: Engineering test harness demonstrates that Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs produce identical page boundaries for 95% of synthetic streams within 10ms variance
Under injected transient network failures (packet drop, 1s disconnect), the adapters resume streams and deliver pages without duplicate payloads in 99% of trials when deduplication helper enabled
Memory usage: client SDKs demonstrate median additional memory < 8MB per active stream under default config in benchmark suite
Latency: first-page time-to-emission meets < 250ms p50 for 1k token streams in hosted environment
Backward compatibility: existing cursor-based integrations continue to work unchanged; CI suite includes a regression test verifying previous paged endpoints
Telemetry emitted: fragment_reassembly_ms, page_emission_ms, retry_count, backpressure_events are visible in Console and mapped in the release dashboard
Docs and migration guide published: PRD -> developer docs, code examples for Python/TS/Go, and a migration checklist
